body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The story a lot of families are talking about today is the break-in at North High School, where a parent says a man got onto campus during school hours and walked off with her son's bike and trading cards. It's a cool, clear Friday — 57 degrees at Meadows Field on the way to a high near 69, air quality good at 39, and no weather alerts anywhere in the county.

## The Kern Overnight

It was a busy night across the county, starting with two weapons calls that came in within a couple of hours of each other. Around 8:17 p.m., officers were sent to Worthington Avenue and Lowell Drive in north Bakersfield for a woman reported to be hitting vehicles with a baton-style stun gun and screaming; she was described as wearing a black hoodie and dark pants. A little over two hours later, at 10:29 p.m., deputies headed to the Love's truck stop on Boron Frontage Road North for a man reported to be walking through the parking lot with a sword.

Earlier in the evening, just after 8 p.m., officers took a secondhand report of two men in masks and all black chasing a woman in the 6200 block of Brahma Street in south Bakersfield. Domestic violence calls came in through the night from an apartment in the 2700 block of North Chester Avenue, from Baker Street in east Bakersfield, from Beardsley Avenue, from the 3400 block of Anderson Street in southeast Bakersfield, and from one address where the man involved was already the restrained party on a served protective order.

Just after midnight, officers were sent to a cell phone store at Niles Street and Glenwood Avenue, where a man who reportedly walked out without paying for phones was chased by other customers; the call came in as an attempted robbery. Around 1:20 a.m., officers stopped a car and several people ran, and a perimeter was set before two of them were caught. A traffic stop just before 2 a.m. turned into a pursuit that ran eastbound at 42 mph and then north at 18 mph before dead-ending into a cul-de-sac near the 1300 block of Chamberlain Avenue in east Bakersfield, where one person was taken into custody. And at 3:37 a.m., deputies went to a Union Pacific train at Comanche and Edison after the crew reported someone had cut the train's air flow regulator, forcing an emergency stop.

## Today's weather

It's 57 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, and we're headed to a high near 69 with a low around 53 tonight — a mild, easy fall Friday. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and the air quality index is sitting at 39, which is good. No active fires are being reported in the county. After Thursday's rain — more on that below — today looks like the kind of afternoon worth taking outside.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a Bakersfield family is questioning security at North High School after a man allegedly got onto campus during school hours and stole their 15-year-old son's belongings.** Donnie Jones told the station that three of his Yu-Gi-Oh decks and a bicycle given to him by a close friend were taken from the bike rack after classes. His mother, Tania Diaz, said a campus police officer told her the suspect entered the school and hid in a restroom until students were dismissed — a detail that has her worried about how easily an unauthorized adult could get in.

**According to KGET 17, incumbent Supervisor Zack Scrivner and challenger Ayon met Thursday night for a debate that was quarrelsome at times but agreeable at others.** The exchange gave voters in that district a direct look at the two candidates ahead of the election. We'll have more on the substance of the debate as coverage develops.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Kern County set an October 22 rain record, with 0.43 inches falling in just two hours.** It's the kind of quick, heavy burst that can overwhelm storm drains and slick up Highway 99 in a hurry, and it's a reminder that our rainy season tends to arrive all at once. The record fell on a single day; the season is just getting started.

**KGET 17 also reports that Zack Scrivner's closed-door diversion hearing drew protesters to the Kern County courthouse.** The hearing itself was held out of public view, but the crowd outside made clear that plenty of people in the county are following the case closely. We'll keep watching for what comes out of the proceeding.

**23ABC reports that a Lamont auto shop is now offering free vehicle pickup for customers who are staying home amid immigration enforcement.** Lamont Auto Repair owner Emanuel Espinoza told the station the shop started the service after noticing the streets looked like a ghost town and business dropped off, and that calls have been coming in steadily since. The Rapid Response Network of Kern confirmed one person was detained by ICE in Lamont on Tuesday; one customer, who asked not to be shown on camera, said she found the shop's offer on social media and is grateful for the help.

**And 23ABC reports that rain changed the plans but not the spirit at McFarland High School, where homecoming went on without its traditional city parade.** With rain in the forecast, the parade was called off two days out, so students moved the celebration onto campus under this year's "Hollywood" theme — each class wrote and produced short films and performed on the floor, and the juniors took home the trophy. Activities director Ezenia Lorta said students had been preparing for at least a month and the energy had to go somewhere.

## Something good

There's genuinely encouraging news on the health front: Kern County has recorded zero fentanyl-related child deaths for two years, according to a new report. That's a milestone worth pausing on — it reflects real, sustained work by the people trying to keep this drug away from kids, and it's a meaningful sign for the safety of local families. Whatever is being done right, it's worth keeping up.

And in McFarland, the homecoming story is its own small bright spot — a town that lost its parade two days before the big week and turned a gym full of bleachers into something the younger kids will remember anyway.

## Coming up this week

It's a full weekend at the Fox Theater. Tonight, Friday, October 23, comedian Henry Cho brings The Empty Nest Tour to the Fox. Saturday, October 24, brings two shows in one day: Fred Armisen's "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome" and BLADE RAVE, both at the Fox. Sunday, October 25, illusionist REZA brings Edge of Illusion to the same stage, and Monday, October 26, J & J Investigations leads Ghost Tours at the Fox — a fitting way to close out October.

Looking a little further out, the Fox's Cults & Classics season pass for 2026–2027 is on sale now, a good option if you like your classics on a big screen. We don't have any public meetings on the calendar for the coming week yet; when agendas post, we'll get them into the brief. In the meantime, enjoy the mild weather, keep an eye out for slick spots where Thursday's rain is still draining, and have a good Friday.

top.title: Family questions local high school's security after man allegedly sneaks on campus, steals teen's belongings
